name: vix_mean_reversion_intraday_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, intraday VIX deviations anchored to the day's session-open level reflect the cumulative net put-buying pressure since 09:15. When VIX has risen > 3% from its day-open value and begins declining (2 consecutive 5-second bars), options market makers who sold puts during the fear wave start buying NIFTY futures to reduce their delta-hedge — generating a 15-30 second spot rally. The day-open anchor (vs. a rolling window) matters because institutional hedgers target their book to morning risk levels; deviations from that anchor are the directional signal, not short-term oscillations. The bearish mirror fires when VIX has been steadily crushed from open (complacency) and the first VIX uptick signals returning put demand, preceding a NIFTY correction.

indicators.name: vix_day_open
indicators.formula: VIX close at first bar of each day (09:15), forward-filled through the session
indicators.purpose: Day-open VIX anchor — identical concept to original. No period to scale: it is a fixed daily reference, reset each session. Institutional hedgers benchmark their intraday gamma exposure to this morning level, making it the natural reference for 'how much has fear changed today'.

indicators.name: vix_change_from_open_pct
indicators.purpose: Intraday VIX % deviation from day-open anchor — the primary trigger. Threshold 3% is carried directly from the original (same signal, now applied to NIFTY options directly without beta adjustment). Captures CUMULATIVE intraday fear, distinguishing this strategy from vix_mean_reversion_v1 which measures only the most recent 10-minute spike.

indicators.name: vix_ema_360
indicators.purpose: 30-minute VIX intraday trend line (360 bars × 5s = 30 min = same time window as original's EMA(30) on 1-min bars). Used as CONTEXT FILTER: is VIX above or below its session trend? A context filter at 30-min horizon is appropriate regardless of our 30-120s hold time — it answers 'is the current deviation anomalous vs the day's own trend?' rather than detecting the trigger itself.

indicators.name: vix_reversal_2bar
indicators.purpose: 2 consecutive declining 5-second VIX bars (10 seconds) — reversion onset confirmation. Original used 3 bars of 1-min (3 minutes). At 5s resolution, 2 bars (10 seconds) is sufficient to distinguish genuine reversal from tick noise while still entering before 50% of the bounce is consumed. Using 3 bars (as in vix_mean_reversion_v1) adds 5 more seconds of lag — unacceptable for the faster intraday-drift signal this strategy is built on.

indicators.name: nifty_open_return_pct
indicators.purpose: NIFTY % return from day-open — coherence filter ensuring the spot index has actually moved in the expected direction (VIX spike should coincide with NIFTY down from open; VIX crush with NIFTY up). Replaces original's stock-beta calculation: no beta needed when trading NIFTY index itself.

conditions: vix_change_from_open_pct > vix_spike_threshold (VIX > 3% above day-open — cumulative fear elevated)
vix_close > vix_ema_360 (VIX above 30-min EMA — still above intraday trend, room to revert)
nifty_open_return_pct < -nifty_move_threshold (NIFTY down > 0.3% from day-open — spot confirms fear)
vix_reversal_2bar == True (2 consecutive 5s bars of VIX declining — reversion has started)
buy_ce.confirmation: All 4 conditions simultaneously. vix_reversal_2bar is the timing trigger; the others gate it to only genuine elevated-fear days.

conditions: vix_close < vix_ema_360 (VIX below 30-min EMA — below intraday trend)
nifty_open_return_pct > nifty_move_threshold (NIFTY up > 0.3% from day-open — spot confirms complacency)
vix_uptick_2bar == True (2 consecutive 5s bars of VIX rising — re-hedging started)
buy_pe.confirmation: Complacency reversal: VIX bottomed and ticked up while NIFTY is extended above open.

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points at delta ~0.5. If NIFTY moves another 8 spot points against the trade after VIX begins reverting, the day-open deviation is deepening rather than mean-reverting — the thesis is invalidated for this session. NIFTY 30s typical range is 2-5 option pts; 4 pts is at the upper end, giving the trade room for micro-pullbacks before the trend resumes.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points = ~14 NIFTY spot points. When VIX reverts from a 3%+ day-open spike, NIFTY typically recovers 20-35 spot points in the first 60-90 seconds of the reversion. Targeting 14 spot pts captures ~50% of the median first-leg recovery, consistent with 2-minute time stop. Risk-reward 1:1.75.
exit.eod_rule: flatten at 14:30 IST — matching original's session cutoff; post-14:30 VIX dynamics are dominated by end-of-day hedging rolls, not mean reversion

filters.vix_filter: Core — VIX must have deviated > 3% from day-open before any entry; vix_ema_360 provides trend context
filters.time_filter: Entries only 10:00-14:30 IST (600-870 min) — let VIX stabilize for 45 min after open; no late-day entries
filters.volume_filter: None — NIFTY index is always liquid; VIX is a derived level, not volume-dependent
filters.trend_filter: Counter-trend by design (VIX spike → NIFTY bounce); no additional trend alignment needed
filters.spread_filter: N/A — limit order execution at candle close, no bid-ask spread

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — VIX intraday mean-reversion via option MM delta-hedging is structural, driven by market microstructure rather than behaviour

adaptation_notes: Original traded top-10 high-beta Nifty50 stocks using VIX deviation from day-open as a proxy for market fear. Converted to NIFTY index options directly: (1) Removed stock-beta calculation — NIFTY itself has beta=1.0 to Nifty50, no adjustment needed. (2) VIX EMA period kept at 30-min equivalent (360 5s bars) as it is a context filter, not a trigger. (3) Confirmation compressed from 3 minutes (original's 3 bar × 1-min) to 10 seconds (2 bars × 5s) to enter at the reversion's leading edge rather than midpoint. (4) Day-open anchor retained exactly — this is what differentiates this strategy from vix_mean_reversion_v1 (which uses a rolling 10-min spike window). (5) Session start moved to 10:00 IST to match original's stabilization filter.
weaknesses: VIX > 3% from day-open events occur only 5-8 times per month — very low trade frequency, capital-inefficient standalone
In genuine macro shocks (geopolitical, RBI surprise), VIX spike is one-directional and the 2-bar reversion is a head-fake; strategy takes repeated stop-losses
Day-open VIX anchor becomes stale if the global risk environment changes dramatically mid-session (e.g., US data at 14:00 IST)
First 30 minutes of vix_ema_360 warmup period has unreliable EMA; combined with 10:00 start filter this is managed but not eliminated
